primary_access.title: Structural abnormalities of the cornea and lid resulting from collagen V mutations.

reference_review.review_notes: The unchanged cache is abstract-only. Original author-uploaded article text was read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/7341155/ (DOI:10.1167/iovs.05-0771): Methods/Patients and Table 1, printed page 566; Human Ocular Phenotype, pages 567–568. One COL5A2 exon-skipping patient is distinguished from seven COL5A1 patients and the Col5a1 mouse experiments. This is external indexed full-article text access, not a downloaded full PDF or figure-pixel read. The source index separates its retrieval hashes from the cache hash.

primary_access.title: Downregulation of extracellular matrix-related gene clusters during osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow- and adipose tissue-derived stromal cells.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete selected abstract read: COL5A2 occurs in a downregulated human stromal-cell ECM-gene cluster. Full Methods were not recovered; expression is not treated as direct protein localization. Independent human ECM data support the retained location.

primary_access.title: The collagen family members as cell adhesion proteins.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete selected collagen-review abstract read; bounded full recovery failed. Exact COL5A2 type-XI passage remains unverified, so that NAS complex row is UNDECIDED. Independently established ECM location is retained without claiming the missing passage was read.

Selected full-cache body passages and original Table 1 were read. The table is omitted from the local extraction but is present in the saved indexed original PMC page at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3003457/ (DOI:10.1101/cshperspect.a004978). Its type-V and type-XI rows plus the body paragraph on molecular isoforms support the source-specific type-V replacement. The separate direct HTML retrieval returned a challenge and supplies no table evidence. The article surveys the collagen family; a shared repository copy does not make it a COL18A1-specific paper.

primary_access.title: Regulation of endodermal differentiation of human embryonic stem cells through integrin-ECM interactions.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual original Results/Figure 1 and Methods (Cellular microarrays; Differentiation of hESCs) were read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3569984/ (DOI:10.1038/cdd.2012.138). Commercial human collagen V was applied as whole matrix protein, and SOX17/DNA factorial analysis reports a negative differentiation effect. Alpha2(V), its receptor and an endogenous pathway were not isolated. Fibronectin/vitronectin receptor perturbations are separate experiments.

primary_access.title: Extracellular matrix signatures of human primary metastatic colon cancers and their metastases to liver.

reference_review.review_notes: Selected human extraction/MS Methods/Results and both original workbook COL5A2 rows were read. The P05997-containing group has 95 total unique peptides; two worksheet views are not two independent assays and grouping is not isoform resolution.

primary_access.title: Extracellular matrix remodelling in response to venous hypertension: proteomics of human varicose veins.

reference_review.review_notes: Selected actual human vein extraction/MS Methods/Results and original Figure 3 caption were read; the caption explicitly names CO5A2. Supplement recovery yielded images or access failures, not a target workbook. No bar values or figure pixels were read. An initially misdirected unrelated PMC response was excluded and preserved with an explicit disposition.

primary_access.title: Glycoproteomics Reveals Decorin Peptides With Anti-Myostatin Activity in Human Atrial Fibrillation.

reference_review.review_notes: Protected selected partial cache remains unchanged. Genuine original PMC article was separately recovered; selected human-heart extraction/MS passages and Table I alpha2(V) row were read. Positive GuHCl input detection is distinct from blank enriched glycoprotein/glycopeptide columns.

primary_access.title: Comprehensive proteomic characterization of stem cell-derived extracellular matrices.

reference_review.review_notes: Protected selected partial cache remains unchanged. Genuine original PMC full article was separately recovered and selected Methods/Results plus Table I COL5A1/2 group read. Human stem-cell/fibroblast matrices and shared human/bovine peptide assignment limit chain-specific inference; no isolated alpha2 force assay is claimed.

primary_access.title: Proteomic characterization of human multiple myeloma bone marrow extracellular matrix.

reference_review.review_notes: Protected original abstract remains unchanged. Authentic original S2 and five S3 COL5A2 rows and headers were independently inspected. S2 nd summaries do not negate the single new-diagnosis and relapsed detections in S3. Original full main Methods were not newly recovered; supplement access is explicit.

primary_access.title: Characterization of the Extracellular Matrix of Normal and Diseased Tissues Using Proteomics.

reference_review.review_notes: Selected partial main Results/Discussion protocol text read. Exact COL5A2 supplementary target data remain unavailable: purported workbook and additional article routes returned HTML challenges. No negative target-table finding is inferred. Independent matrix/assembly evidence supports the retained biological class and location.

primary_access.title: The Chemistry and Biology of Collagen Hybridization.

reference_review.review_notes: Selected actual review paragraphs on collagen composition and assembly read. This is contextual synthesis, not a new chain-specific human experiment; direct target grounding comes from mutation and matrix studies.

primary_access.title: Mutations of the alpha2(V) chain of type V collagen impair matrix assembly and produce ehlers-danlos syndrome type I.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete genuine abstract reports human alpha2(V) mutations, matrix-assembly impairment and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Bounded external attempts did not yield full Methods. Core retention uses this explicit positive abstract plus independent actual mouse assembly evidence, without inventing original construct or assay details.

primary_access.title: A single base mutation in COL5A2 causes Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type II.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete genuine abstract identifies the human COL5A2 mutation and type-V collagen disease. Full original Methods were not recovered. Positive target evidence is retained with access limits, not rejected from title or abstract emphasis.

primary_access.title: Interaction of Smads with collagen types I, III, and V.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete normal abstract and exact mouse Col5a2 Q3U962 IPI donor records support a positive SMAD-interaction premise. The abstract describes fetal-murine-library yeast two-hybrid and GST pull-down assays for collagen types I, III and V; the alpha2(V) identification comes from curator records. Full construct Methods remain unavailable. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2003.09.130. No native human feedback mechanism or absence of binding is inferred.

primary_access.title: Development of a functional skin matrix requires deposition of collagen V heterotrimers.

reference_review.review_notes: The unchanged publication cache is abstract-only. Selected original full-body Methods, Results and Discussion were read separately at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC480903/ (DOI:10.1128/MCB.24.13.6049-6057.2004): Protein Analysis; Results/Figures 3–5. Metabolic labeling is distinct from purified collagen/Coomassie densitometry (wild-type 1.6:1 versus mutant 15.5:1 alpha1:alpha2). Sparse alpha2 remains; assembly, secretion and stability are not completely separated. No figure-pixel inspection is claimed. Full-text availability records this genuine external access, not the cache extraction level; public locators and separate hashes are in the source index.

followup_4938.source_specific_type_XI: GO:0005592 defines alpha1(XI), alpha2(XI) and alpha1(II), whereas COL5A2 encodes alpha2(V). The full PMID:17876790 passage remains unavailable, so its precise NAS assignment cannot be resolved against that definition. V/XI hybrid biology is real: the original PMID:16431952 Introduction describes alpha2(V) with alpha1(XI) in vitreous hybrids, without establishing the strict GO:0005592 composition. Keep this source-specific question UNDECIDED; the available PMID:21421911 Table 1 independently supports a type-V correction for its separate TAS row.
followup_4938.available_Table1_correction: Original PMID:21421911 Table 1, accessed in the indexed PMC article, lists alpha2(V) under type V and lists the V/XI hybrid as alpha1(XI), alpha1(V), alpha3(XI). Its accompanying body text likewise identifies alpha1(V) in those hybrids. Current GO:0005592 specifies alpha1(XI), alpha2(XI), alpha1(II); GO:0005588 explicitly includes alpha2(V)-containing type-V heterotrimers. This available source therefore supports MODIFY to type V. The correction does not deny other tissue-specific hybrid assemblies.

followup_4938.SMAD_scope: GO:0046332 requires binding a SMAD signaling protein; it does not require a demonstrated native signaling pathway. Three current mouse Col5a2 Q3U962 IPI records cite PMID:14559231, and the official Ensembl protein link resolves to that ortholog. The primary abstract reports fetal-mouse-library yeast two-hybrid and GST pull-down binding of collagen V to SMADs. Alpha2(V) attribution rests on those curated donor records because the sequence-defined full assay constructs were not recovered. Retain this positive transferred interaction as non-core, without asserting native human intracellular feedback or rejecting binding solely because mature collagen is extracellular.
followup_4938.matrix_assay_scope: GO:1903225 covers reduction of endodermal differentiation. Human embryonic-stem-cell microarrays in PMID:23154389 tested commercial whole human collagen V during Wnt3a/Activin-A induction and normalized SOX17 to DNA. The factorial analysis reports a negative collagen-V effect. This is an experimentally applied matrix effect, supporting the existing contextual annotation to its alpha2(V) constituent; it is not an isolated alpha2-chain assay. The receptor and endogenous developmental mechanism remain unresolved, and the separate fibronectin/vitronectin receptor perturbations are not COL5A2 experiments.
